description: The M4 Competition is BMW M's statement piece, a coupe built around a twin-turbocharged inline-six and tuned with one goal: making every back road feel like a closed circuit. The wide kidney grille, muscular haunches, and quad exhaust finishers give it a presence that's unmistakable even at a standstill, and this example's M Sao Paulo Yellow finish only sharpens that effect. Inside, carbon-backed sport seats and a driver-canted cockpit keep the focus exactly where it belongs. At 8,500 km, it has been exercised enough to prove its dependability, but not so much that it has lost its edge. For a buyer who wants a genuine performance coupe that is equally happy on a Monday commute or a Sunday drive, this is about as complete a package as the segment offers.

The C300 is Mercedes-Benz's case for understated luxury done right. Its Obsidian Black exterior is quietly elegant rather than showy, while the cabin leans into the brand's reputation for craftsmanship, with soft-touch materials, ambient lighting, and a dash dominated by the brand's signature widescreen displays. It rides with the kind of composure that makes long commutes feel shorter, and its turbocharged four-cylinder is tuned more for smoothness than drama. With 12,500 km covered, this C300 has been driven the way it was designed to be: as a comfortable, capable daily companion rather than a garage ornament. It suits a buyer who wants the Mercedes badge and the comfort that comes with it, without needing to shout about either.

The A6 is Audi's executive sedan distilled into a single, confident shape: long proportions, a low roofline, and the brand's signature single-frame grille, finished here in a restrained Daytona Grey. Quattro all-wheel drive underpins its reputation for composed, all-weather confidence, while the cabin's twin-screen MMI setup and Audi Virtual Cockpit bring a genuinely modern edge to the driving experience. Every surface, from the stitched leather to the brushed aluminium trim, is finished the way you would expect from a car built to sit at the top of a boardroom car park. At 6,200 km, it is barely broken in. This is the sedan for someone who wants their car to communicate precision and quiet authority in equal measure.

The Model 3 Performance is Tesla's proof that an electric sedan can be genuinely thrilling rather than merely efficient. Dual motors deliver immediate, uninterrupted power the moment you press the accelerator, and the low centre of gravity from the underfloor battery pack makes it feel planted through corners most sedans would not attempt. Inside, the minimalist cabin is built around a single central touchscreen that controls nearly everything, giving the whole car an uncluttered, almost futuristic calm. Finished in Midnight Silver with only 3,200 km on the clock, it is essentially showroom-fresh. For a buyer ready to make the switch to electric without giving up performance, this is one of the most convincing arguments on the market.

Few silhouettes are as instantly recognisable as the 911's, and this Carrera wears it in a Guards Red that is practically the model's signature colour. The flat-six engine sits over the rear axle exactly where Porsche purists expect it, delivering the distinctive engine note and rear-biased balance that have defined the 911 for generations. Inside, the cabin blends analogue-inspired dials with modern Porsche Communication Management, a combination that feels both timeless and current. With just 1,800 km covered, this car has barely left first ownership, practically new in every way that matters. It is suited to a buyer who wants a genuine sports car icon, not a car that merely borrows the badge.

The Camry Hybrid has built its reputation on one simple idea: dependability that never feels like a compromise. Its petrol-electric powertrain is tuned for effortless efficiency rather than outright pace, making it an easy, relaxed car to live with day to day. The Pearl White finish suits the Camry's clean, understated lines, and the cabin prioritises comfort and simplicity over flash, with supportive seats, a straightforward dash layout, and enough room for a family to travel without compromise. Having covered 15,600 km, this example has proven its reliability without showing real wear. It is the natural choice for a buyer who wants low running costs and long-term peace of mind above all else.

The Civic RS takes Honda's long-standing reputation for sharp, engaging handling and wraps it in a genuinely upscale sedan body. Its turbocharged engine is tuned for responsive, eager acceleration rather than outright brute force, and the sport-tuned suspension keeps it composed through corners without sacrificing everyday ride comfort. The Crystal Black finish and RS-specific styling cues, from the rear spoiler to the sportier bumpers, mark it out from the standard Civic at a glance. Inside, the cabin balances Honda's practical ergonomics with red-stitched sport seats that hint at its more spirited character. At 7,900 km, it is a well-used but far-from-worn example, ideal for a buyer who wants everyday practicality without giving up any driving enjoyment.

There is no mistaking the Mustang GT for anything but what it is: an unapologetic American muscle car. Its naturally aspirated V8 delivers the deep, mechanical soundtrack the nameplate has been known for since the 1960s, paired with rear-wheel drive that rewards a confident right foot. Finished in Race Red with the GT's signature bonnet vents and quad-tip exhaust, it looks every bit as bold as it sounds. The cabin mixes retro-inspired gauges with a modern digital instrument cluster, a nod to six decades of Mustang heritage without feeling dated. With 5,100 km on the clock, this GT is ready to be driven exactly as Ford intended: with confidence, and with a grin.

The Range Rover Sport occupies a rare space: genuinely capable off-road, yet just as at home outside a five-star hotel. Its diesel powertrain is tuned for effortless, torque-rich cruising, and Land Rover's Terrain Response system means the capability underneath is there whenever it is needed, even if it rarely leaves the tarmac. Santorini Black exterior paint and a cabin trimmed in soft leather and real wood veneers give it a hushed, first-class atmosphere that few SUVs can match. Air suspension smooths out everything from motorway expansion joints to gravel driveways alike. With only 4,100 km covered, it is in essentially new condition, a fitting choice for a buyer who wants presence, comfort, and genuine capability in a single vehicle.

The XC60 leads with what Volvo has always led with: safety and thoughtful, human-centred design. Its hybrid powertrain balances efficiency with enough everyday punch for confident overtakes, while the Denim Blue paint and clean Scandinavian lines give it an understated elegance rather than SUV bulk. Inside, the vertical touchscreen and minimalist dashboard reflect a design philosophy built around reducing clutter, not adding it, and the seats are finished with the kind of textile and leather combinations Volvo is known for. Having covered 13,400 km, it is a well-proven example of a genuinely well-rounded family SUV. It is an easy recommendation for a buyer who prioritises safety and calm, considered design over outright drama.

The IONIQ 5 looks like nothing else on the road, and that is entirely the point: its pixel-inspired lighting and cab-forward, retro-futurist silhouette signal that this is Hyundai's clearest statement yet on where electric design is headed. Built on a dedicated 800-volt electric platform, it supports rapid charging that can add meaningful range in the time it takes to grab a coffee. Inside, a dual-screen cockpit and a flat floor, freed up by the absence of a transmission tunnel, create a lounge-like sense of space rarely found in this segment. Finished in Atlas White with just 2,800 km covered, it is practically brand new. This is the SUV for a buyer who wants their electric vehicle to look as forward-thinking as it drives.

The EV6 GT is Kia's performance flagship, and it wears that role with a Runway Red finish that refuses to blend in. Dual electric motors deliver the kind of instant, all-wheel-drive acceleration that used to be the exclusive territory of six-figure sports cars, while the swooping, coupe-like roofline keeps it looking more athletic than the typical crossover. Inside, curved dual displays and a driver-focused control layout give the cabin a genuinely high-tech feel. With only 3,600 km on the odometer, it remains in essentially showroom condition. It is built for a buyer who wants electric performance that is genuinely fun, not just fast in a straight line.

The CX-5 has quietly become the benchmark for what a mid-size SUV can be without a luxury badge attached. Mazda's KODO design language gives it flowing, almost sculptural lines, and the Soul Red Crystal finish is widely regarded as one of the best paint jobs in the segment, shifting depth and tone with the light. Behind the wheel, precise steering and a well-controlled chassis make it feel noticeably more engaging than most competitors, without ever compromising ride comfort. The cabin punches above its price point too, with genuine leather options and tight, rattle-free fit and finish. At 11,800 km, this CX-5 has been well maintained and is ready for a buyer who wants an SUV that feels considered rather than merely practical.

The Golf GTI invented the hot hatch category decades ago, and this generation continues to defend that title. Its turbocharged four-cylinder and sharp, well-weighted steering make it feel genuinely playful on a twisty road, while the tartan-cloth sport seats, a GTI hallmark since the very first model, add a wink of heritage to an otherwise thoroughly modern cabin. Finished in Kings Red with the model's signature red grille trim, it looks purposeful without tipping into boy-racer territory. Practical enough for daily errands but sharp enough for a spirited weekend drive, and with 6,500 km covered, it remains in excellent shape. It is the natural pick for a buyer who refuses to choose between practicality and driving enjoyment.

The X-Trail is built around one priority above all others: making family life easier. Its hybrid powertrain is tuned for smooth, unfussy efficiency, and the boxy, upright shape translates into genuinely useful interior space rather than style-over-substance styling. A full suite of driver-assistance technology, from adaptive cruise control to a 360-degree camera system, takes the stress out of everyday driving, particularly in tight car parks. The Gun Metallic finish is understated by design, letting the SUV's practicality speak for itself rather than chasing attention. Having covered 8,700 km, it remains in strong condition. This is the SUV for a buyer whose priority is dependable, low-drama versatility over outright excitement.

The RX 500h represents Lexus at its most confident: a luxury SUV that pairs hybrid efficiency with genuinely engaging performance. Its turbocharged hybrid powertrain is tuned to deliver both a spirited response when asked for it and near-silent cruising the rest of the time, while the spindle grille and sharply creased bodywork, finished here in Sonic Titanium, give it real road presence. Inside, Lexus's famed build quality shows in every stitch and switch, with quilted leather, real metal accents, and one of the quietest cabins in its class. With only 4,200 km covered, it drives as good as new. It suits a buyer who wants five-star comfort without giving up a genuine sense of occasion behind the wheel.

The Corvette Stingray marked a historic shift for Chevrolet, the first Corvette generation to move its V8 behind the driver rather than in front, chasing the kind of balance previously reserved for exotic supercars costing several times as much. That mid-engine layout gives it razor-sharp turn-in and a low centre of gravity that makes high-speed cornering feel almost effortless. Finished in the marque's signature Torch Red with the Stingray's low, wide stance, it looks every bit the supercar it is benchmarked against. Inside, a driver-wrapped cockpit angles every control toward the person behind the wheel. With just 2,300 km on the clock, this is a car that has barely begun its story, ideal for a buyer chasing exotic-car performance without the exotic-car price tag.

The F-PACE is Jaguar's proof that an SUV can carry genuine sporting pedigree without losing everyday usability. Its diesel engine favours long-legged, torque-rich cruising, well suited to motorway miles, while double-wishbone front suspension gives it noticeably sharper handling than most rivals in the segment. Finished in a British Racing Green that ties directly back to Jaguar's motorsport heritage, it looks distinguished rather than merely large. The cabin wraps occupants in leather and aluminium trim, with the brand's rotary gear selector adding a touch of theatre to every drive. Having covered 9,400 km, it remains in excellent condition. This is the SUV for a buyer who wants their family car to still feel unmistakably like a Jaguar.

The Cooper S proves that a small footprint does not have to mean small character. Its turbocharged engine and go-kart-like handling, a phrase practically invented to describe Minis, make even a short trip to the shops feel like an occasion, while the compact dimensions make it genuinely effortless to park and thread through city traffic. Finished in Island Blue with contrasting white mirror caps and roof, it carries the brand's playful, unmistakable design language. Inside, the circular central display and toggle switches are as much a personality statement as they are functional controls. With 5,700 km covered, it is ready for a buyer who wants a car that is as fun to drive as it is easy to live with.

The Outback has built a loyal following by doing one thing consistently well: going anywhere, in any weather, without fuss. Standard symmetrical all-wheel drive and generous ground clearance mean it is as comfortable on a gravel trail as it is on the motorway, while the raised ride height and boxer engine's low centre of gravity keep it planted through corners most crossovers would not attempt. Finished in a practical Magnetite Grey, its boxy proportions prioritise cargo space and visibility over styling flourishes. Inside, durable, easy-to-clean materials reflect its outdoors-ready ethos. Having covered 8,100 km, this Outback is ready for its next adventure, well suited to a buyer whose weekends involve trailheads as often as they involve tarmac.
